item.title: Timeline set for long-awaited Dromod works
item.description: It's been confirmed that improvement works at Dromod train station will go out to tender in the coming weeks. Work is also expected to commence on the site in the third quarter of the year. Planning permission was previously granted for a number of measures at the station. item.title: Local hospitals among those with lengthy waiting lists
item.description: Two local hospitals have been categorised as having an elevated risk in relation to patient waiting lists. According to data from the Irish Patients Association, Sligo University Hospital and Roscommon University Hospital were ranked in the top 10 for busiest waiting lists as of last month. Just over 3,000 adult patients were on the hospital waiting list in Sligo last month with almost 600 on the list for over a year according to the report. item.title: Litter louts leave their mark in Strokestown
item.description: Disgust has been expressed in Strokestown after a number of dumping incidents in recent days. A significant amount of clothes were found outside a clothes bank on Church Street in the town. In a post shared on social media, Strokestown Tidy Towns group condemned the act. Advertisement They say they are "hoarse from asking for more to be done by Roscommon County Council."

item.title: Dixon's to the fore on Monaghan night Navigation trial
item.description: Elijah and Abraham Dixon came out on top in the Night navigation trial on Saturday night. The Novice crew topped the leader board on 4 penalties. item.title: Overcrowding problems persist at local hospitals
item.description: Sligo University Hospital was the fourth most overcrowded in the country today. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Tuesday's figures show there 57 patients waiting for a bed there this morning. Advertisement This included 31 in the emergency department and 26 on wards elsewhere. Meanwhile, there were 25 patients waiting at Portiuncula and 8 in the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar.

item.title: Sinn Féin motion condemns Ireland's handling of Mercosur negotiations
item.description: Sinn Féin are calling on the Government to detail the steps they've taken to oppose the Mercosur Trade Deal. The party is tabling a motion in the Dáil this evening condemning Ireland's negotiations at EU level. Sinn Féin's Agriculture Spokesperson Martin Kenny has accused Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael of trying to 'ride two horses'. item.title: Cabinet signs off on new €75 million funding package for An Post
item.description: Cabinet has today signed off on €75 million in funding to support the postal network over the next five years. The allocation had been announced in the Budget and represents an increase of €5 million per year. It's been described as a crucial support for An Post which will help to prevent further post office closures. item.title: Athlone waste facility set to reopen
item.description: An Athlone waste facility closed by the Health and Safety Authority is set to reopen this week. The Barna waste facility, located on the University Road closed in early December. At the time of the closure, the local authority said the closure was not an action of Westmeath County Council.
